name: Sea teal
lede: Sea teal is one of ColorHub's own curriculum colors rather than a name from the classic dictionaries, and it shares its exact hex with another library name, Light teal tone.

sections.title: A curriculum name, not a dictionary one
sections.body:
Sea teal is one of ColorHub's own curriculum colors rather than a name drawn from Ridgway, Maerz and Paul, or the ISCC-NBS census [1]. Our data flags it as also appearing in a Japanese traditional color list, but records no kanji, romanization, or date for that entry, so the connection stays undocumented here [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[capri-blue]] and [[cadet-blue]], at The Inter-Society Color Council's nearest 1955 block describes a color this hue as a light greenish blue [1]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[blue-munsell]], 6.5 ΔE away, bluer and more vivid [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Sea teal in 31 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.1 percent, as photographed [2]. It sits as a mid-tone more often than as a highlight or shadow, and shares canvases with paintings also carrying [[teal]] at 237 times the rate chance alone would predict [2]. United States paintings carry it a little above the archive's base rate, France and Belgium not far behind [2]. The counts are a computed color match on varnished, photographed canvases, never a pigment identification [2].
